notice: Hypothetical example audit. The property, people, firms and figures are all invented.
title: Kestrel House, Northampton

issues.original: £1,750,000 (One Million, Seven Hundred and Fifty Thousand Pounds)
issues.corrected: £1,850,000 (One Million, Eight Hundred and Fifty Thousand Pounds)
issues.explanation: The signed valuation statement in section 10 gives £1,750,000, in figures and in words; the Executive Summary, the yield analysis and the valuation in Appendix 2 all give £1,850,000. The signed figure looks left over from an earlier draft, and it is the one figure the lender relies on. Please confirm which is correct.

issues.original: We are of the opinion that the Property is not suitable security for secured lending purposes, subject to the comments made within this report.
issues.corrected: We are of the opinion that the Property is suitable security for secured lending purposes, subject to the comments made within this report.
issues.explanation: The Executive Summary says the Property is not suitable security; section 11 (Suitability as Loan Security) concludes that it is. One of them is wrong, and the lender reads the summary first.

issues.original: Our valuation reflects a net initial yield of 8.50%, having regard to the contracted income of £168,000 per annum.
issues.corrected: Our valuation reflects a net initial yield of 8.50%, having regard to the contracted income of £168,000 per annum.
issues.explanation: The £168,000 includes £24,000 from Unit B. That lease has not been signed, does not start until 1 November 2026 (after the valuation date), and is to Kestrel Kitchen Limited, which shares a director with the Borrower. A lender would normally expect income like this to be left out, or flagged clearly, because it is not yet secure and may not be on arm's-length terms. Without it the income is £144,000, and at the same 8.50% yield the value would be about £1,586,000, some £264,000 lower. Should Unit B be valued as vacant, or should the report tell the lender plainly that the yield depends on this lease?

issues.original: Our opinion of Market Rent for Unit C is based on £625 per room per calendar month across 14 lettable rooms, on the terms of an assured shorthold tenancy for 12 months.
issues.corrected: Our opinion of Market Rent for Unit C is based on £625 per room per calendar month across 14 lettable rooms, on the terms of an assured shorthold tenancy for 12 months.
issues.explanation: The Market Rent for Unit C is built on 14 lettable rooms, but the HMO licence quoted in section 6 permits 12. At £625 per room per month, 12 rooms gives £90,000 a year, not £105,000: £15,000 a year less, and it is the rent the valuation capitalises when the lease ends in 2029. Which room count is right?

issues.original: HMO licence (West Northamptonshire Council) – provided
issues.corrected: HMO licence (West Northamptonshire Council) – expired 14 August 2026; renewal application pending
issues.explanation: Sources of Information lists the HMO licence as provided, but section 6 says it expired on 14 August 2026 and no licence was in place at the valuation date. The upper floors are 12 rooms let as an HMO, so the lapse affects the operator's lease and 46% of the income. It should be stated in the summary and the Key Issues, with the assumption the valuation makes about renewal.

issues.original: [AV note: MV at last instruction (March 2025) was £2,100,000 – check movement before issue]
issues.corrected: [AV note: MV at last instruction (March 2025) was £2,100,000 – check movement before issue]
issues.explanation: An internal drafting note is still in the report, and it gives a previous Market Value of £2,100,000, £250,000 above this valuation. It needs to come out before issue, and the lender may ask about the fall.

issues.original: This Report and Valuation has been checked by A. Valuer MRICS, Director, Example Firm LLP, and a member of the RICS Valuer Registration Scheme.
issues.corrected: This Report and Valuation has been checked by [name of checking valuer], [position], Example Firm LLP, and a member of the RICS Valuer Registration Scheme.
issues.explanation: The report names A. Valuer, the signing valuer, as the person who checked it, and the signature block in section 12 still reads "[Name of Checking Valuer]" and "[Position]". The checking valuer needs to be named in both places.

issues.original: The upper floors are let to Northgate Living Limited on a five-year lease from January 2025 at an annual rent of £75,000, fixed for the term.
issues.corrected: The upper floors are let to Northgate Living Limited on a five-year lease from January 2025 at an annual rent of £78,000, fixed for the term.
issues.explanation: The valuation commentary gives Unit C's rent as £75,000 a year; the tenancy schedule and the valuation in Appendix 2 both use £78,000. The figure in the commentary is the one to correct, unless the schedule is wrong.

issues.original: Unit A (Ground Floor Retail), Mercer Convenience Stores Ltd: 35,800
issues.corrected: Unit A (Ground Floor Retail), Mercer Convenience Stores Ltd: 38,500
issues.explanation: The valuation in Appendix 2 capitalises £35,800 for Unit A; the tenancy schedule and the valuation commentary give the rent as £38,500. It appears two digits have been swapped. If £38,500 is right, the income valued is £2,700 a year too low. Please confirm which is correct.

issues.original: Unit B is currently trading as Kestrel Kitchen, a café with seating for approximately 30 covers.
issues.corrected: Unit B is currently trading as Kestrel Kitchen, a café with seating for approximately 30 covers.
issues.explanation: Unit B is described three ways: trading as Kestrel Kitchen in section 4, "vacant, under offer" beneath the accommodation schedule, and let on a lease not yet completed that starts after the valuation date in section 6. Which was the position at the valuation date? The income and the yield depend on it.
Unit D's lease expired on 31/03/2026, before the valuation date, and the report does not say whether the tenant is holding over or has a new lease. Which is it? The car park is valued as if let.

issues.original: Key Issues Requiring Clarification: None identified.
issues.corrected: Key Issues Requiring Clarification: None identified.
issues.explanation: The Key Issues box says "None identified", but the tenancy schedule shows Unit D's car park lease expired on 31/03/2026, six months before the valuation date. Should it be listed there?

issues.original: The Environment Agency's Long Term Flood Risk service identifies the Property as being within an area at high risk of flooding from surface water.
issues.corrected: The Environment Agency's Long Term Flood Risk service identifies the Property as being within an area at high risk of flooding from surface water.
issues.explanation: Section 4 records a high risk of surface water flooding, but the Executive Summary and the Key Issues box say nothing about it. A lender would expect it in both, with a comment on insurance.

issues.original: The Property is Grade II listed, being a former telephone exchange dating from 1934.
issues.corrected: The Property is Grade II listed, being a former telephone exchange dating from 1934.
issues.explanation: The building is Grade II listed and its upper floors were converted to a 12-room HMO in 2023, but the report does not say whether listed building consent was granted for the conversion. Works without consent to a listed building are a criminal offence and can be enforced against any owner. Has consent been seen, or should it go to the lender's solicitors?

issues.original: We have adopted a Market Rent of £40,000 per annum for Unit A, equating to £19.93 per sq ft overall.
issues.corrected: We have adopted a Market Rent of £40,000 per annum for Unit A, equating to £19.93 per sq ft overall.
issues.explanation: The adopted £19.93 per sq ft for Unit A is above every retail letting the report cites, which run from £14.50 to £17.25 per sq ft. What supports the step up?

issues.original: 14 Derngate, Northampton NN1 1TT | Sold: November 2026 | £1,850,000 | 7.95% NIY
issues.corrected: 14 Derngate, Northampton NN1 1TT | Sold: November 2026 | £1,850,000 | 7.95% NIY
issues.explanation: This sale is dated November 2026, after the valuation date of 30 September 2026 and the report date of 9 October 2026. Evidence that did not exist at the valuation date cannot support it. Is the date wrong, or should the comparable come out?

issues.original: Westbury Court benefits from a prominent corner position opposite the main entrance to the retail park, with the A45 within half a mile.
issues.corrected: Westbury Court benefits from a prominent corner position opposite the main entrance to the retail park, with the A45 within half a mile.
issues.explanation: The location section describes Westbury Court, a retail park and the A45. None of them is the subject property, which is Kestrel House on Mercer Street. The paragraph looks carried over from another report.

issues.original: We have made status enquiries of Northgate Living Limited by way of a Creditsafe report, which details a credit score of 41 (moderate risk) as at 14/11/2026.
issues.corrected: We have made status enquiries of Northgate Living Limited by way of a Creditsafe report, which details a credit score of 41 (moderate risk) as at 14/11/2026.
issues.explanation: The credit report is dated 14/11/2026, after the valuation date (30 September 2026) and the report date (9 October 2026). The date is wrong, or the enquiry was made after the report was signed.

issues.original: Total Net Internal Area: 697.30 7,405
issues.corrected: Total Net Internal Area: 697.30 7,405
issues.explanation: The accommodation schedule adds up to 7,505 sq ft, not the 7,405 sq ft stated. The stated total is 100 sq ft short. Please confirm which is correct.

issues.original: The Property is arranged over basement, ground and two upper floor, with the principle access from Mercer Street.
issues.corrected: The Property is arranged over basement, ground and two upper floors, with the principal access from Mercer Street.
issues.explanation: "floor" should be "floors", and "principle" should be "principal".

issues.original: Unit A benefits from a return frontage to Kestrel Lane an a rear service door to the yard.
issues.corrected: Unit A benefits from a return frontage to Kestrel Lane and a rear service door to the yard.
issues.explanation: "an" should be "and".

issues.original: We have assumed that the units benefit from the necessary planing consents for their current uses.
issues.corrected: We have assumed that the units benefit from the necessary planning consents for their current uses.
issues.explanation: "planing" should be "planning".

compliance.label: Red Book report contents
compliance.caveat: Fixed checks against the Red Book's minimum report contents (VPS 6). They assume a full Red Book valuation, so check your terms of engagement: if this report was instructed on a different basis, some items may not apply.

rows.label: Valuer named and signed
rows.heading: (a) Identification and status of the responsible valuer
rows.quote: A. Valuer MRICS, RICS Registered Valuer
rows.standardSays: The report must include the signature of the individual responsible for the valuation assignment.

rows.label: Professional designation
rows.heading: (a) Identification and status of the responsible valuer
rows.quote: A. Valuer MRICS, RICS Registered Valuer
rows.standardSays: In all cases the signatory's professional designation (for example MRICS) must be made clear.

rows.label: Objectivity and competence statement
rows.heading: (a) Identification and status of the responsible valuer
rows.quote: We confirm that the valuer has acted with objectivity and has the knowledge, skills and understanding to undertake the valuation competently.
rows.standardSays: A statement confirming that the valuer is in a position to provide an objective and unbiased valuation, and is competent to undertake the valuation assignment.

rows.label: Previous involvement declared
rows.heading: (a) Identification and status of the responsible valuer
rows.quote: Example Firm LLP valued the Property for a previous lender in March 2025. We do not consider that this gives rise to a conflict of interest.
rows.standardSays: Where there has not been any other material involvement, a statement to that effect must be made in the valuation report.

rows.label: Statement of market knowledge and skills
rows.heading: (a) Identification and status of the responsible valuer
rows.quote: The valuer has sufficient current local and national knowledge of the particular market to undertake the valuation competently.
rows.standardSays: A statement should be made that the valuer and/or the valuer's firm has sufficient current local, national and international (as appropriate) knowledge of the particular market, and the skills and understanding to undertake the valuation competently.

rows.label: Client and intended users
rows.heading: (b) Identification of the client and any other intended users
rows.quote: This report is addressed to Example Lender Limited and may be relied upon by it and its successors in title.
rows.standardSays: The report must be addressed to the client. The source of the instructions and the identity of the client must be stated, if different from the addressee. Other known users of the report are to be named.

rows.label: Purpose of the valuation
rows.heading: (c) Purpose of the valuation
rows.quote: The valuation is required for secured lending purposes, in connection with a proposed loan secured on the Property.
rows.standardSays: The purpose of the valuation assignment must be clearly stated.

rows.label: Property and legal interest identified
rows.heading: (d) Identification of the asset(s) or liability(ies) valued
rows.quote: We have valued the freehold interest in the Property, subject to and with the benefit of the occupational leases.
rows.standardSays: The asset or liability must be clearly identified, distinguishing the asset itself from the interest or right of use in it. The legal interest should be stated.

rows.label: Basis of value with its full definition
rows.heading: (e) Basis(es) of value adopted
rows.quote: Market Value: the estimated amount for which an asset or liability should exchange on the valuation date between a willing buyer and a willing seller in an arm's length transaction.
rows.standardSays: The basis of value, together with its definition, must be stated in full in the report.

rows.label: Valuation date stated
rows.heading: (f) Valuation date
rows.quote: Valuation Date: 30th September 2026
rows.standardSays: The valuation date must be stated.

rows.label: Valuation, inspection and report dates distinguished
rows.heading: (f) Valuation date
rows.quote: Date of inspection: 24 September 2026. Valuation date: 30 September 2026. Date of report: 9 October 2026.
rows.standardSays: Where the valuation date, the date of inspection and the date of the report differ, these dates must be clearly distinguished in the report.

rows.label: Extent of inspection, with date and anything not accessed
rows.heading: (g) Extent of investigation
rows.quote: We inspected the common parts, both ground floor units and four of the 12 rooms on the upper floors. The roof was not accessed.
rows.standardSays: The report must record the date and extent of any inspection, including reference to any part of the property to which access was not possible.

rows.label: Nature and sources of information
rows.heading: (h) Nature and source(s) of the information relied upon, including sources of key data and inputs used
rows.quote: Tenancy schedule – provided
rows.standardSays: The nature and source of the information relied on and the extent of any steps taken to verify that information must be disclosed.

rows.label: Rationale for data reliability and quality
rows.heading: (h) Nature and source(s) of the information relied upon, including sources of key data and inputs used
rows.standardSays: The rationale for the valuer's opinion of the general reliability and quality of the important data, inputs, modifications and assumptions must be documented in the report.

rows.label: Assumptions and special assumptions in full, agreed with the client
rows.heading: (i) Assumptions and special assumptions
rows.quote: Where a lease incorporates a break option, we have assumed that the tenant exercises their option.
rows.standardSays: All assumptions and any special assumptions must be set out in the report in full, together with any reservations, and a statement that they have been agreed with the client.

rows.label: Special assumptions repeated at the valuation conclusion
rows.heading: (i) Assumptions and special assumptions
rows.naReason: No special assumptions are made in the valuation.
rows.standardSays: Both the valuation conclusion and the executive summary (if provided) should explicitly set out all special assumptions.

rows.label: Restrictions on use, distribution and publication
rows.heading: (j) Restrictions on use, distribution and publication of the report
rows.quote: This report is for the use of the addressee only and for the purpose stated. No responsibility is accepted to any third party.
rows.standardSays: The valuer must state the permitted use, distribution and publication of the valuation.

rows.label: Statement of compliance with the standards
rows.heading: (k) Confirmation that the valuation has been undertaken in accordance with IVS and/or RICS Red Book Global Standards
rows.quote: The valuation has been undertaken in accordance with the RICS Valuation – Global Standards, effective from 31 January 2025.
rows.standardSays: The valuer should provide confirmation that the valuation has been undertaken in accordance with IVS and/or the RICS Valuation – Global Standards, which incorporate IVS, and (where applicable) the relevant RICS national or jurisdictional supplement. (RICS words this one as 'should', not 'must' — but its absence is a defect on any lender panel, so it is treated as required here.)

rows.label: Approach, method and principal reasoning
rows.heading: (l) Valuation approach and reasoning, including any valuation method(s) and complex or proprietary model(s) used
rows.quote: We have adopted the investment method, capitalising the contracted income to the lease events and the Market Rent thereafter.
rows.standardSays: The report must make reference to the approach(es) adopted, the method(s) and model(s) applied, key inputs used and the principal reasons for the conclusions reached.

rows.label: Value in words as well as figures
rows.heading: (m) Amount of the valuation or valuations
rows.quote: £1,750,000 (One Million, Seven Hundred and Fifty Thousand Pounds)
rows.standardSays: In the main body of the report, the opinion of value must be provided in words, as well as in figures.

rows.label: Date of the report
rows.heading: (n) Date of the valuation report
rows.quote: DATE OF REPORT: 9 OCTOBER 2026
rows.standardSays: The date on which the report is issued must be included.

rows.label: Material valuation uncertainty
rows.heading: (o) Commentary on any material valuation uncertainty (MVU) in relation to the valuation where it is essential to ensure clarity on the part of the valuation user
rows.naReason: The report does not report the valuation as subject to material uncertainty.
rows.standardSays: Where the degree of uncertainty in a valuation falls outside any parameters that might normally be expected and accepted, it must be expressly signalled in the report, with proportionate commentary on the circumstances as at the valuation date. A standard general caveat is not sufficient, and stating a range of values is not an acceptable way of disclosing material uncertainty.

rows.label: Limitations on liability
rows.heading: (p) A statement setting out any limitations on liability that have been agreed
rows.quote: Our liability is limited as set out in our terms of engagement at Appendix 1.
rows.standardSays: A statement setting out any limitations on liability that have been agreed.

rows.label: Significant ESG factors considered
rows.heading: (q) Significant environmental, social and governance (ESG) factors used and considered
rows.quote: The Environment Agency's Long Term Flood Risk service identifies the Property as being within an area at high risk of flooding from surface water.
rows.standardSays: Valuers must identify, report and document the consideration of significant ESG factors and any impact on the valuation conclusion and/or rationale.

rows.label: Wording barred by the Red Book
rows.heading: Terminology (VPS 6 s1.8)
rows.meaning: None of the wording the Red Book bars was found in the report.
rows.standardSays: The terms 'certificate of value', 'valuation certificate' and 'statement of value' should not be used.
